values.note: $20 a night, with the fee and registration procedure posted at the campground kiosk. A Recreation Passport is required for vehicle entry to every state forest campground.

fees.source: https://www.michigan.gov/recsearch/sfcampgroundsa-m/meadcreek ('Overnight fees ($20 for most sites) and registration procedures are posted at the information kiosk at each campground'; 'A Recreation Passport (park pass) is required for vehicle entry into all state park and forest campgrounds') + https://www.michigan.gov/dnr/things-to-do/camping-and-lodging/state-forest-campgrounds/amenity-table (Mead Creek State Forest Campground, Schoolcraft: 9 sites, $20), read 2026-10-25

values.note: Drinking water from a hand-pump well. Boat launch on the Manistique River inside the campground, reached over a narrow wooden bridge; the water level fluctuates.

facilities.source: https://www.michigan.gov/recsearch/sfcampgroundsa-m/meadcreek ('There are vault toilets.' 'Potable (drinking) water is available from a hand-pump well.' 'A boat launch is located on the Manistique River within the campground. Please note that the water can fluctuate quite a bit. Drivers must use a narrow wooden bridge to access the boat launch.'), read 2026-10-25

booking.source: https://www.michigan.gov/recsearch/sfcampgroundsa-m/meadcreek ('No reservations. Sites available on a first-come, first-served basis.' 'Camping is limited to a 15-day maximum stay.') + amenity table ('Reservable at MiDNRReservations.com' no), read 2026-10-25

values.note: 'Nine sites accommodate tents and small trailers' (the DNR's standard state forest wording; no maximum length posted). Sites 1-4 are riverfront; the rest sit on a bluff. One camping unit and six people per site.

sites.source: https://www.michigan.gov/recsearch/sfcampgroundsa-m/meadcreek ('Nine sites accommodate tents and small trailers'; 'Riverfront sites (1-4) provide immediate access to the water and picturesque views, while the remaining sites are perched on a bluff.'; 'One camping unit and six people are allowed per site.') + amenity table (9 campsites), read 2026-10-25

note: Rustic MI DNR state forest campground where Mead Creek meets the Manistique River, 6 mi SW of Germfask via M-77 and County Road 436 (Schoolcraft County); managed by Indian Lake State Park. Walleye, bass and pike; the river is an easy, undeveloped paddle. ORVs and snowmobiles may ride between the campground and the trails (Trail 8 is adjacent). --Claude
summary: DNR page + SF amenity table: 9 tent/small-trailer sites (count confirmed; length silent), $20 at the kiosk + Recreation Passport, no electric, vault toilets, hand-pump water, first-come only, 15-day maximum (all confirmed). Season (open all year) already manual and matches. A general rustic campground (type 'rustic') with ORV/snowmobile trail access (Trail 8 adjacent), not described as an ORV trail camp; no equestrian wording. The note's 'fits a 23-ft rig' is not stated by the DNR and was dropped. Note trimmed of field restatements.
